context.objective: Document how this process works, including controls and what remains unresolved.

turns.text: Financial Close & Reporting Overview routes the quarterly close to the detailed processes. It has no separate execution or completion criteria and grants no extra approval authority.
Which detailed close or reporting process would you like to walk through?

I'd like to document the routing itself. For workbook preparation and account support the overview sends work to FA-13, cash reconciliation to FA-16, statement generation and tie-out to FA-12 and binder assembly to FA-15A. Before work begins, each workstream must be assigned to its documented detailed process and a routing or assignment record retained.
Who assigns each workstream to its detailed process?

The overview does not specify who makes the routing assignment, who checks it, or the firmwide close calendar owner. Each detailed process defines its own controls. At overall close level the documented review chain is Fund Accountant, Controller, Director and client; the client approves the completed package. This chain is not evidence that any one of those roles owns routing.
Where is the routing or assignment record kept?

I can't identify a controlled location for that assignment record from this overview. Recordkeeping otherwise follows the detailed processes. The current approved calendar, checklists and their owners aren't confirmed. We preserve the client's approved method with its source, effective date, owner/approver and exceptions; the mostly blank toolkit does not authorize choosing a method.
Does this routing apply the same way across the quarterly closes you cover, or does it vary?

Q1–Q3 are usually unaudited; Q4 is generally audited with footnotes, subject to the client and engagement. Client methods, templates, delivery and milestones differ. A prior client's answer must be verified for the current entity and period and can't be generalized to another engagement. Organization-wide due dates and escalation timeframes are not confirmed.
How does the Q4 audit and footnote work change the routing to detailed processes, if at all?

The route for audited financial statements and the agreement check is still FA-12, with engagement-specific footnote work. Binder support goes to FA-15A and year-end audit support to FA-15B. I cannot identify a separate Q4 routing workflow from this overview. An unresolved upstream issue keeps the dependent statement, binder or investor reporting step open. The investor-reporting and portal release SOP has not been identified.
What can go wrong if a workstream is not assigned to its documented detailed process before work begins?

Without a documented assignment, execution and release can be assigned inconsistently; an unsupported item can block downstream client, auditor, tax or investor use. The quarter's intended outputs include a reconciled workbook, approved statements, evidence of review, complete binder and released investor packages. Those outputs and detailed procedures govern completion, not a separate sign-off for the routing overview.
When a client’s milestones or delivery method differs, what changes in the workstream assignments, if anything?
